neighbours.label: the disease-category modifier in a medical name, just before 'Disease(s)' (Kid|ney, Infect|ious, Insect-B|orne, Liver, Chronic ...)
fire: He is a fellow in the Division of Infectious Diseases at the university hospital.
The clinic treats patients with chronic kidney disease and diabetes.
She chairs the national foundation for liver disease research.
Mosquito control is central to preventing vector-borne diseases.
The report describes the burden of disease in low-income countries.
Our department of Kidney Medicine runs a dialysis unit.
Researchers at the institute study infectious disease outbreaks in cattle.
Fatty liver disease is increasingly common among teenagers.
quiet: He is a fellow in the Department of English at the university.
The chef cooks red kidney beans with rice and spices.
She ordered chicken liver pate at the French restaurant.
Her infectious laugh filled the whole auditorium.
The report describes the burden of debt in low-income countries.
Our department of Sleep Studies runs a weekend workshop.
Researchers at the institute study weather patterns in the mountains.
Fatty foods are increasingly common among teenagers.

notes: card: peaks on 'ney' in Kidney, 'ious' in Infectious, 'orne' in Insect-Borne, ' Liver', ' Chronic', ' Sleep', 'Burden of' (Disease) in medical institution and report names. Near misses use the same words outside a disease name.
